annotationRationale: The two reviewed methods for the identical AMC 10A question are retained with their method-specific credits. Both combine exhaustive counting with rotation and coordinate-reflection properties. Group notation and partial-state bookkeeping do not provide a useful additional route here.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate for counting compositions of rigid transformations. No area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The ordered-sequence interpretation gives 125 possibilities. Independently, six successful sequences use no reflections and six use two reflections, giving 12, choice A. The examples and key agree; there is no figure conflict.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: For 2020_AMC_10A_Q23, classify-by-reflections and force-the-last-move are both retained and independently valid for this identical question. The historical classify-reflection-count route is merged into classify-by-reflections. The historical count-composition-states route has no stored worked explanation and is reasonably omitted because state bookkeeping adds little beyond the retained pair-counting route. AoPS group notation gives an equivalent classification, not a necessary additional method.
review.annotationCheck: Combined counting is appropriately assessed, with rotation properties and coordinate reflections supporting both methods. Removing the modular-congruence support ID is reasonable because the small quarter-turn calculation is explained directly.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate for counting compositions of rigid transformations. No area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Different distances from the fixed origin prevent exchanging the nonzero vertices. Orientation requires zero or two reflections. The rotation-only multisets are exactly (1,1,2) and (2,3,3), contributing three orders each. With two reflections, a quarter-turn exchanges axes and fails; a half-turn requires one reflection in each axis. All six orders of those sign changes work, giving 12.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The exact shared question and method are correctly credited. Both the inherited aops-reference-2020_AMC_10A_Q23 and the current-question AoPS reference are retained. Reuse of the project explanation is authorized by the supplied provenance; source-informed-original correctly distinguishes it from an official MAA solution.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The orientation split is motivated, and the axis-exchange argument handles every placement of the single rotation. The sign-change explanation establishes both necessity and sufficiency without requiring a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h232 matches the exhaustive case count and arrangement counts; cnm_245 matches rotations; cnm_136 matches coordinate-sign reflections. No unsupported group-theory prerequisite is used.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three supplied native-topic links fit the written counting, rotation and coordinate-reflection work. This exercise uses relevant parts of those topics rather than establishing complete mastery.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The supplied rotation links provide partial rigid-motion overlap, and 8.G.A.3 and 6.NS.C.6b support coordinate sign changes within their narrower scope. Experimental verification and full congruence-standard coverage are not demonstrated. No accepted US counting link is supplied.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three immediate nodes are supported. The assessed counting role and supporting geometry roles accurately describe this derivation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Fixing the three vertices forces the identity, and inverse closure makes a pair completable exactly when its composition is allowed. Rotation pairs contribute 9 minus 3 identities, mixed pairs contribute four half-turn/reflection pairs, and distinct reflection pairs contribute two. Quarter-turn/reflection pairs are unavailable diagonal reflections. Thus each of 12 pairs determines one successful triple.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The shared force-the-last-move method and its underlying live-reference-2020_AMC_10A_Q23 are both retained, alongside the current LIVE reference. The pair-counting strategy matches the supplied material, while the project reuse and third-party status are honestly identified.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The unique-inverse reduction is explained before counting. Every pair type, excluded identity and unavailable diagonal reflection is accounted for, and the final correspondence prevents double counting.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h232, cnm_245 and cnm_136 directly support the pair classification and coordinate compositions. The identity and inverse observations are explained elementary consequences, not unexplained advanced machinery.
